items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang expressed optimism regarding the AI market, stating that recent turmoil will pass as technology benefits outweigh investor concerns. Speaking in Berlin, he noted the transformative impact on industries globally. While the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell for eight days and Nvidia shares dropped, Huang urged investors to focus on long-term fundamentals rather than short-term volatility.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Optimistic on AI Market Despite Turmoil

items.summary: Tim Cook, Apple's executive chairman, expressed strong appreciation for China during a recent visit. He described the nation as dynamic, vibrant, and optimistic, specifically highlighting its AI ecosystem. Cook noted that the environment was inspiring significant optimism for the future. These glowing remarks were made as part of his broader appreciation for the country.
items.title: Tim Cook praises China's dynamism and AI ecosystem during visit

items.summary: Tesla unveiled a new Roadster capable of flying, though its road legality remains uncertain. Reservations require a deposit of 5,000 dollars, with a total reservation amount of 2.5 million dollars. Production is expected in 2028, but no delivery date is confirmed.
items.title: Tesla Unveils Flying Roadster with Uncertain Road Legality and 2028 Production

items.summary: A Tesla driver claimed he fell asleep while using driver-assistance technology before crashing into a parked California Highway Patrol vehicle on Interstate 80. Two CHP officers from Solano County were seriously injured in the incident, which was captured by the car's dashboard camera. The injured officers were transported to a hospital by local residents.
items.title: Tesla Driver Claims Sleep Caused Crash Into CHP Vehicle

items.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves fell $8.6 billion to $726 billion during the week ended Oct 9, marking the fifth consecutive weekly decline. The Reserve Bank of India intervened to stabilise the rupee, which strengthened 1.9% against the dollar. Measures including a dedicated dollar window for state-owned oil companies aim to ease speculative pressure, though underlying demand for US dollars remains high.
items.title: India's Forex Reserves Drop as RBI Defends Rupee Amid Dollar Pressure

items.summary: Vedanta Resources Chairman Anil Agarwal expressed awe at Tesla CEO Elon Musk's demonstration of a redesigned Roadster performing aerial maneuvers. Agarwal noted that concepts once found in science fiction are now becoming reality, praising the synergy between bold entrepreneurship and scientific development. Musk confirmed the vehicle uses rocket-style thrusters developed with SpaceX, though Tesla has not specified a target price or practical flight range.
items.title: Vedanta Chairman Praises Tesla Flying Car Innovation

items.summary: Brazil's Amazon recorded its lowest annual deforestation rate since 1988, with 3,335 square kilometres cleared between August 2025 and July 2026, according to INPE. This represents a 41.8 per cent drop from the previous year. Environment minister João Paulo Capobianco called it a 'stratospheric drop,' while climate advocate Márcio Astrini hailed it as a historic achievement. The figures bolster President Lula's environmental targets ahead of the October 25 presidential runoff against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who has pledged to strengthen environmental oversight.
items.title: Brazil's Amazon Deforestation Hits Record Low Amid Election Battle

items.summary: OpenAI has hired Graham Seamans, previously leading sales at Elon Musk's xAI unit, to head its cybersecurity business. This move follows recent hires from SpaceX's AI divisions, including staff from Cursor. Seamans, who joined xAI in August 2025, aims to expand OpenAI's commercial reach through enterprise sales and new revenue streams like advertising ahead of a potential public listing. OpenAI declined to comment on the specific details of the hire.
items.title: OpenAI Hires SpaceX Sales Executive Graham Seamans for Cybersecurity Role

items.summary: Apple's upcoming HomeView smart display, priced at $299, features facial recognition and a 7-inch screen. However, the author notes a significant limitation: its photo features rely on iCloud Photos. This design makes the device difficult to recommend to the 1.5 billion people who use Google Photos, potentially leaving the display feeling empty without a steady supply of fresh images from that source.
items.title: Apple HomeView Faces Google Photos Limitation

items.summary: Brazil's government reports a record decline in Amazon deforestation, with rates falling 41.8% in the year to July 2026. President Lula credits tightened monitoring and penalties for the drop, while Environment Minister Joao Paulo Capobianco called the decline 'absolutely stratospheric.' The data arrives ahead of a presidential run-off where the rainforest's future is a key issue.
items.title: Brazil Reports Record Drop in Amazon Deforestation Ahead of Election

items.summary: Chinese authorities are seeking public input on a revised export control list that would include AI, biomedicine, and photovoltaics technologies. The Ministry of Commerce and the Ministry of Science and Technology propose changes covering 40 technologies. Exporters must register these items before shipping. Public consultation runs from October 16 to November 15, 2026.
items.title: China Consults on Export Controls for AI, Biomedicine and Solar Tech

items.summary: The Financial Times reported that Anthropic is offering Blackstone a yield exceeding 10 percent to finance a chip deal involving $9 billion in debt. This funding is backed by five-year lease payments. Reuters could not immediately verify the report.
items.title: Anthropic Offers Blackstone High Yield for Chip Financing

items.summary: Nanning serves as a key logistics hub in China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, facilitating rail transport of goods across borders to ASEAN markets. Located on the New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor, the Nanning International Railway Port links southwest China with regional trade routes. This improved connectivity is expected to generate new opportunities, strengthen local industries, and foster closer regional ties.
items.title: Nanning Railway Corridor Connects China and ASEAN Markets

items.summary: Anthropic signed a lease with EverWind for a data center at Point Tupper, Nova Scotia, marking its first Canadian agreement, an executive stated. Separately, EverWind plans to invest more than C$10 billion in the campus. Anthropic spent $7.33 billion last year and prepares for a US IPO that could value it at more than $2 trillion.
items.title: Anthropic Signs Lease for First Canadian Data Center in Nova Scotia

items.summary: Data from Brazil's INPE shows Amazon deforestation fell 42% to 3,335 square kilometers in the 12 months ended July 31, 2026, the lowest level on record. The Cerrado also hit a record low of 5,516 sq km. Progress accelerated since President Lula took office in 2023, though political uncertainty and a brewing super El Niño event threaten future gains.
items.title: Amazon Deforestation Drops to Record Low Amid Political and Climate Challenges

items.summary: Travel booking platform Klook Technology filed to withdraw its US IPO plans on Oct 16, citing current market conditions as the deciding factor. A spokesperson stated the company will continue evaluating the right time for a listing. The move joins other companies deferring IPOs in 2026 due to volatile markets and cautious investor appetite.
items.title: Klook Technology Files to Withdraw US IPO Plans Amid Market Volatility

items.summary: Databricks has announced that multi-statement transactions are now generally available for its lakehouse architecture, supporting both Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg tables. This feature enables organizations to run complex, multi-step workflows with atomic guarantees directly on open, governed data, eliminating the need for separate warehouse systems. By integrating with existing tools and offering row-level concurrency, the update aims to reduce operational complexity and data movement. Customers like Fivetran and Accolade have adopted the technology to ensure data consistency and reliability in their production environments, allowing them to modernize workflows without maintaining duplicate systems.
items.title: Databricks Announces General Availability of Multi-Statement Transactions on Lakehouse

items.summary: Velislava Hillman and Peter G. Kirchschläger argue that society has entered an 'Age of Hypertrophy,' where the relentless pursuit of abundance in information and production has become counterproductive. They suggest that while AI and digital tools promise efficiency, they may induce 'cognitive debt' by outsourcing mental effort. Citing an MIT study and a 2025 trial, the authors note that reliance on AI for writing and studying correlates with weaker brain connectivity and lower knowledge retention. The article warns that this trend threatens to atrophy human capacities, replacing meaningful struggle with hollow efficiency and leaving future generations ill-equipped to endure hardship.
items.title: The Age of Hypertrophy: When Abundance Undermines Human Capacity

items.summary: The DeLorean Motor Company announced its entry into the Airspeeder International Series, an electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft racing competition. The team, named the DeLorean Airspeeder Team, will compete starting in November 2026. DMC clarified that this racing team is separate from Delorean Aerospace, another startup developing an eVOTL prototype. While DMC plans to design future vehicles with student engineering teams, the initial entry will use an Alauda-developed Mk3C aircraft. The announcement follows Tesla CEO Elon Musk's unveiling of a Roadster EV capable of brief flight, sparking comparisons between the two companies' ambitions in aviation technology.
items.title: DeLorean Motor Company Enters Electric Flying Car Racing Series

items.summary: The Netherlands' digital infrastructure inspectorate warns that faulty updates or cyberattacks on cloud platforms could destabilize the grid by controlling inverters and batteries simultaneously. The regulator notes current EU laws only partly cover these backend systems. It proposes stricter standards and includes companies controlling remote capacity under NIS2, regardless of size.
items.title: Dutch Regulator Warns of EU Cyber Gap for Cloud-Controlled Home Batteries

items.summary: Samsung plans to launch the Galaxy F70 5G in India on October 18 for under 20,000 rupees. The device features a 50MP camera, 5000mAh battery, and AI capabilities, with details revealed via a Flipkart microsite.
items.title: Samsung to launch Galaxy F70 5G in India under 20,000 rupees on October 18

items.summary: Politico reports that Anthropic representatives pitched a draft AI safety bill to Capitol Hill lawmakers. The proposal allows the government to block models posing risks of over $1 billion in damages or injuries to more than 50 people. An Anthropic spokesperson stated the bill aligns with the company's "Advanced AI Framework."
items.title: Anthropic Quietly Proposes AI Safety Bill to Lawmakers

items.summary: Starlink responded to Reliance Industries' statement regarding Elon Musk's comments on the Indian market. Starlink affirmed it has secured all requisite government approvals after working with regulators for over five years. Reliance stated it welcomes competition but emphasized adherence to Indian laws. The dispute follows Musk's accusations of discrimination by Indian oligarchs, which the communications ministry rejected as baseless.
items.title: Starlink and Reliance Clash Over India Market Entry Amid Regulatory Scrutiny

items.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met with Israeli President Isaac Herzog in Baku on October 15, 2026, during the Seventh Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia. Herzog highlighted the long history of exchanges between the two peoples and affirmed Israel's commitment to the one-China policy. Wang recalled historical cooperation during World War II and noted that bilateral relations have developed steadily since diplomatic ties were established more than 30 years ago. Both leaders discussed regional peace, with Herzog emphasizing Israel's stance on national security and Wang stressing the importance of the two-state solution and full access to the Gaza Strip.
items.title: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi Meets Israeli President Isaac Herzog

items.summary: An older video resurfaced on social media showing a Chinese bride surprising her groom with an ASUS ROG Astral RTX 5090 graphics card. The clip, widely reshared on X, captures the groom's emotional reaction as he realizes the gift. Users labeled the couple "relationship goals," noting the gesture acknowledges his gaming passion despite the hardware's high price and scarcity.
items.title: Chinese Bride Gifts Husband RTX 5090 GPU on Wedding Day

items.summary: The think tank GTRI states that a US waiver on Russian oil tariffs is temporary and lacks certainty. GTRI founder Ajay Srivastava warns India to avoid permanent trade concessions. The waiver, issued by Trump under the Graham Act, allows the US to withdraw it at any time to leverage trade negotiations.
items.title: Think tank warns India on temporary US tariff waiver

items.summary: A Delhi court issued bailable warrants against YouTuber Dhruv Rathee regarding a 2018 defamation case stemming from a video alleging the BJP IT cell attempted to bribe someone. The complainant, Vikas Sankrityayan, initiated proceedings after summons remained unserved for years. Rathee was previously summoned in July 2019. A next hearing is scheduled for October 17, 2026. Rathee also faces a separate suit over a video regarding religious sentiments.
items.title: Delhi Court Issues Warrants Against YouTuber Dhruv Rathee in 2018 Defamation Case

items.summary: Jio Platforms is set to launch its IPO on October 21, priced between Rs 1,065 and Rs 1,119 per share, with trading closing on October 23. Grey market indicators suggest a potential listing price of Rs 1,340. Brokerage firm Emkay recommends subscribing, citing Jio's market leadership and technology capabilities, while SBI Securities estimates a post-issue valuation of Rs 20,117 per subscriber. Both firms highlight risks including regulatory changes and competitive pressure. The company plans to use proceeds to repay borrowings, aiming to reduce leverage.
items.title: Jio IPO pricing and broker valuations attract market attention

items.summary: British authorities indicated that Kiran Kaur, an Indian woman jailed for helping her son fatally stab a student, could face deportation after her early release. The Home Office plans to deport foreign criminals soon, though Kaur's specific case was not named. Her son received a life sentence, and both are appealing. Police conduct regarding the victim is also under investigation.
items.title: Indian woman jailed for son's stabbing faces possible deportation

items.summary: US President Donald Trump issued an executive order waiving sanctions, restrictions, and duties under the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act. Citing national interest, he submitted a certification to Congress regarding the waiver. The act previously empowered the administration to impose sweeping sanctions on Moscow and tariffs on major Russian oil purchasers, including China and India.
items.title: Trump Waives Russia Iran Sanctions Citing National Interest

items.summary: US President Donald Trump signed an executive order pausing a law allowing 100% tariffs on India and four other nations purchasing Russian oil. The waiver serves US national interests before the 30-day implementation period concludes. India's Ministry of External Affairs stated it remains committed to energy security through diversified sourcing.
items.title: Trump Pauses Tariff Law on India and Others Buying Russian Oil

items.summary: US President Donald Trump issued an executive order waiving sanctions, restrictions, and duties under the Graham Act regarding Russian oil and gas. He certified to Congress that this action serves the national interest. The waiver allows the purchase of Russian energy by nations such as China and India, reversing previous measures that targeted these sectors.
items.title: Trump Waives Sanctions and Tariffs on Russian Oil and Gas Purchases

items.summary: Apple and OpenAI are engaged in a trade secrets lawsuit where Apple seeks to inspect devices of former employees who moved to OpenAI. Apple argues there are only a few bad apples, while OpenAI denies the charges and claims Apple is trying to stop employees from joining a rival. The judge has ordered OpenAI to collect forensic images of 14 employees' devices and fast-track evidence.
items.title: Apple and OpenAI Clash Over Trade Secrets and Device Inspections

items.summary: Marine Le Pen, leader of France's National Rally, is campaigning for the 2027 presidential election on a platform that includes ending financial assistance to Ukraine and cutting France's contributions to the EU budget. Speaking in Brussels, she stated that France could only sustain funding for six months due to the perilous state of its public finances. Zelenskyy criticized this stance, arguing that the price of peace is not as high as the value of lives. Experts note that while France has committed an estimated €27 billion to Ukraine since 2022, cuts to EU-level funding would have a greater impact than bilateral aid reductions. Le Pen also proposes capping France's net contribution to the EU budget at €5 billion a year, down from €8 billion, a move rejected by France's National Assembly. Her proposals contrast with those of Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, who advocates continued support for Kyiv.
items.title: Marine Le Pen Campaigns to Cut EU Funding and End Ukraine Aid

items.summary: Left-wing groups protested outside Delhi Police headquarters against recent detentions and alleged police brutality. Simultaneously, the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau released a report on a 2023 Mumbai jet crash citing pilot errors. In student politics, the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad secured victories in Odisha universities, prompting Union Home Minister Amit Shah to congratulate them. India also rejected UN criticism regarding civil liberties at the General Assembly.
items.title: Left Groups Protest Delhi Police Action Amid Student Election Victory

items.summary: West Bengal BJP chief Samik Bhattacharya stated that Sandip Ghosh's bail does not establish innocence. He argued the legal relief reflects technical considerations rather than exoneration. Bhattacharya noted that while public opinion may view Ghosh as involved, the law operates independently of emotion. The Supreme Court granted bail citing prolonged custody and slow trial progress.
items.title: Bengal BJP Chief Says Ghosh Bail Does Not Prove Innocence

items.summary: The teaser for Shah Rukh Khan's film King is scheduled to release on November 2, 2026, coinciding with the actor's birthday. The movie, directed by Siddharth Anand and produced by Red Chillies Entertainment, features an ensemble cast including Deepika Padukone and Anil Kapoor. It is set to premiere in theaters on December 24, 2026, and may be dubbed in six languages.
items.title: Shah Rukh Khan's King Teaser Release Date Announced

items.summary: Finshots released a weekly wrapup discussing several major business developments. The article details China's dominance in the global EV battery market, noting that the nation produces over 75% of worldwide batteries, a position reinforced by 2015 subsidy rules. It also covers the 2026 Nobel Prize in Economics awarded to Robert Hall and Michael Woodford for their work on inflation and interest rates. Additionally, the piece explains new Indian GST reforms aimed at simplifying business operations and examines the challenges Starlink faces entering the Indian market against established providers like Jio and Airtel. Finally, it reports that the Indian government has approved a ₹52,878 crore deal to sell IDBI Bank to Fairfax.
items.title: Finshots Weekly Wrapup Covers Global Business News

items.summary: An Oregon teacher tackled a teenager who opened fire on a special educational needs class at Silver Rail Elementary in Bend. A bystander, Kaylub Giamanco, entered the school and shot the suspect multiple times, killing him. Police identified the 16-year-old suspect as a former student. The teacher, Meghan Lambert, and three children were killed. Giamanco, a 36-year-old carpenter, saved lives but was traumatized. Officials praised both the teacher and Giamanco for their heroic actions.
items.title: Oregon Teacher and Bystander Intervene in School Shooting

items.summary: Aditya Chakrabortty hosts a podcast episode featuring Michael Gove, discussing his political journey and the challenges facing the British right. The episode includes suggested reading on Gove's past writings, the decline of the Conservative Party, and the economic impact of Brexit. Various authors and historians are recommended for further insight into British politics and the Conservative Party's evolution from Thatcher to Sunak.
items.title: Podcast explores Michael Gove's political career and the state of the British right

items.summary: US President Donald Trump signed an executive order waiving a new sanctions package on Russia shortly before it took effect, citing national interest. This move follows criticism of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and a controversial diesel deal between the US and Russia. Zelenskyy warned that sanctions could eventually extend to Ukraine's banking system and chemical industry.
items.title: Trump Waives Russia Sanctions Amid Diesel Deal and Zelenskyy Criticism

items.summary: Half Yours, the previous year's Melbourne Cup winner, suffered a nasty fall late in the Caulfield Cup with about 200 metres to go in the 2,400m race. The horse went down hard, sending jockey Mark Zahra into the turf. While the horse returned to its stall and was described as "all OK" by Racing.com, stewards noted Zahra and jockey Jye McNeil were conscious and alert but transported to hospital for further assessment. Trainer Tony McEvoy reported the horse had suffered some abrasions but looked OK.
items.title: Melbourne Cup winner Half Yours suffers nasty fall in Caulfield Cup

items.summary: Over five trading sessions ending October 16, the Sensex gained 3.11% or 2,257 points to close at 74,729. Amid a broader market rally, around 22 BSE 500 stocks advanced in each session. Researchers identified 15 stocks that gained consistently, delivering cumulative returns ranging from 5% to 25% during the period.
items.title: Sensex Rises as 15 Stocks Gain for Five Days

items.summary: The Delhi Traffic Police announced traffic restrictions in specific areas of Delhi, including south Delhi's Chittaranjan Park and Greater Kailash-II, effective from Friday, October 16, until Tuesday, October 20. These curbs, implemented due to Durga Puja celebrations, apply daily from 4 pm to 12 am. Affected routes include the Outer Ring Road, Lala Lajpat Rai Marg, and Lal Bahadur Shastri Marg. The police urged commuters to use Delhi Metro services and avoid parking near pandals to manage expected heavy footfall and congestion.
items.title: Delhi Traffic Police impose curbs near CR Park and GK-2 for Durga Puja

items.summary: In 1939, physicist Bibha Chowdhuri published an article describing experiments conducted in 1938 to visualize cosmic radiation. Working with DM Bose, she exposed photographic plates soaked in samarium sulphate to cosmic rays at various altitudes in Calcutta, Darjeeling, and Sandakphu. While Calcutta plates were damaged, two plates from Sandakphu revealed 30 star-like tracks indicating nuclear disintegration. Chowdhuri and Bose developed methods to distinguish particle tracks, contributing to research that later aided Cecil Powell’s Nobel Prize-winning work. The study highlighted the utility of photographic emulsions over cloud chambers for detecting rare nuclear events. Chowdhuri continued her research using photographic and camera-based methods until retiring in 1976, leaving a legacy in particle physics visualization.
items.title: Physicist Bibha Chowdhuri Used Photography to Visualize Invisible Cosmic Rays in 1930s India

items.summary: Deputy Louise Doublet criticized the government for ending a free fruit trial in primary schools, citing rising living costs. The education minister ended the scheme due to low consumption and wastage. Doublet argued the trial did not measure cost-of-living benefits and called for more investment in healthy, locally grown food to assist families. She also supported extending funded school meals.
items.title: Jersey Politician Calls for Food Funding Amid Cost-of-Living Pressures

items.summary: King Mohammed VI formally appointed Morocco's first woman-led government on Friday, led by Prime Minister Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri. Her party, the Authenticity and Modernity Party, formed a coalition holding 210 of the parliament's 395 seats. The new cabinet retains several ministers from the previous administration and includes seven women. Mansouri outlined an ambitious program to address citizen expectations, focusing on cost of living, employment, and inequality while preparing for the 2030 World Cup co-hosted with Spain and Portugal.
items.title: Morocco Appoints First Woman-Led Government Under King Mohammed VI

items.summary: Help a Guernsey Child marked its 25th anniversary by noting that families face changing pressures. Since 2001, the charity provided over £1.2m in support. Alex Jenner stated that while needs have shifted, the organization's purpose remains ensuring children are not disadvantaged. The charity now focuses more on individual cases rather than large community projects.
items.title: Help a Guernsey Child Marks 25 Years Amid Changing Family Needs

items.summary: Police in Oregon identified a teenage gunman who killed four people at a school in Bend. A father, Kaylub Giamanco, shot the gunman dead after a teacher tackled him. Police Chief Mike Krantz praised the father and teacher as heroes. President Trump and the NRA also commended Giamanco's use of a legally held weapon. Gun control advocates condemned the ease of firearm access.
items.title: Oregon Police Praise Heroism After School Shooting

items.summary: Many NHS organisations in England are rejecting Palantir's patient data technology, citing better or equal alternatives. While some health bodies noted the £330m platform improved surgery scheduling, others described it as duplicative or retrograde. Following its introduction in March 2024, 16 trusts declared non-use. The government faces a decision on a break clause in the seven-year deal. Critics, including parliamentary committees, argue centralised solutions fail, while Palantir claims the system is successful and exceeds targets. Over 44,000 people have legally objected to data sharing, and concerns persist regarding the company's other contracts.
items.title: NHS Trusts Reject Palantir Patient Data Technology Amid Controversy

items.summary: Financial firms report growing demand for fixed-term annuities, which provide guaranteed income for a set period followed by a lump sum. Standard Life notes rising interest due to higher rates and tax changes, while Canada Life cites a significant surge. These products help individuals fund the gap between stopping work and receiving the state pension, which rises to age 67 in April 2028. However, Legal & General warns that misconceptions remain widespread, with only 35% of surveyed adults correctly identifying lifetime annuities. The products offer flexibility but cannot be changed once set up.
items.title: UK Demand Rises for Fixed-Term Annuities Bridging Retirement Gap

items.summary: Australia reached a record 3.5 GW in annual large-scale solar investment decisions, with the September quarter alone hitting 1 GW. Rooftop solar installations also surged, adding 894 MW in the quarter. Federal Minister Chris Bowen noted that renewable investment has broken annual records and that renewables recently generated more electricity than fossil fuels in the national grid.
items.title: Australia sees record solar investment and rooftop growth in 2026

items.summary: A national memorial service in Canberra marked the 25th anniversary of the SIEV X tragedy, Australia's deadliest known asylum seeker boat disaster. On October 19, 2001, 353 people died when the vessel sank in international waters off Java. Of the dead, 146 were children. The Refugee Action Campaign Canberra organized the service to honor the lives lost and show solidarity with refugees. Organizers noted that while 220 names have been identified and placed on memorial poles, more than 100 names remain unpublicized. The event highlighted ongoing political debates surrounding asylum seekers and the need for compassion.
items.title: Australia marks 25 years since deadliest asylum seeker boat disaster

items.summary: Sanjay Doshi, Head of Investments and Research at Abakkus Mutual Fund, discusses investment opportunities in India's manufacturing, healthcare, and technology sectors. He notes that while large caps offer valuation comfort, mid- and small-cap segments present stronger earnings growth prospects, potentially ranging from 15% to 20%. Doshi emphasizes that valuations must be assessed alongside the sustainability of earnings growth. He advises investors to align SIP allocations with long-term goals rather than reacting to short-term market movements. Doshi highlights that the next generation of wealth creators will be companies converting opportunities into sustainable earnings and cash flows.
items.title: Abakkus Head Sanjay Doshi Outlines India's Next Wealth Creators

items.summary: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda stated he cannot tolerate underlying inflation rising further above 2%. Speaking in Bangkok, he reinforced expectations for further interest rate hikes. While investors anticipate no policy change before the next decision, Ueda emphasized that underlying inflation is already near the target and must not increase.
items.title: BOJ Governor Ueda Warns Against Inflation Rising Above 2%

items.summary: US President Donald Trump issued an executive order waiving tariffs and many sanctions under a new Russia sanctions law while raising duties on Russian goods by 500% and imposing an additional 100% duty on goods from the five largest importers of Russian oil and gas. Meanwhile, EU leaders expressed regret about the US decision to temporarily lift sanctions on Russian diesel. In other news, Washington condemned violence in the West Bank after a Washington Post photographer was attacked, and shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remained about 70% below pre-conflict levels as attacks on commercial vessels continued. Additionally, BTS became the first musical group to surpass 10 billion streams on Spotify in a single year, and the UK government signaled it could intervene in Sky's proposed takeover of ITV's broadcasting business.
items.title: Trump Waives Tariffs Amid Global Tensions and Corporate Moves

items.summary: A UNCTAD report indicates that while AI adoption is global, profits remain concentrated among firms controlling technology design and intellectual property. Analysis of the Nvidia GB200 NVL72 server system shows that 87% of added value is captured by high-value stages, with only 4.3% going to direct production workers. The study urges developing nations to strengthen local suppliers rather than relying on foreign investment.
items.title: UNCTAD Report Reveals AI Profit Concentration at Top

items.summary: Senior IAS officer Kumar Rajiv Ranjan allegedly made derogatory remarks and ordered the suspension of officer Beenish Wani during an October 14 review meeting in Jammu and Kashmir. The incident, sparked by a dispute over the National Rural Livelihood Mission, triggered a political backlash. Kashmir leaders have called for Ranjan's suspension and intervention from the Lieutenant Governor and Chief Minister.
items.title: IAS Officer Allegedly Abused Female Colleague and Ordered Suspension in Kashmir

items.summary: The Home Office refused a visitor visa for Khin Thant Zin, preventing her British great-grandson from meeting his great-grandfather, George Kerr, in the UK. Officials cited insufficient evidence of her ties to Thailand and income. The family, living in Thailand, plans a new application despite the high cost and lack of appeal rights, hoping the baby can still meet his relative at Christmas.
items.title: Home Office Denies British Baby's Great-Grandfather UK Visit

items.summary: Matt Faherty's study argues that the NSF, NIH, and federal government should prioritize metascience to improve outcomes. The report suggests using metascience to test funding reforms, such as shifting to a people-over-projects model. Faherty notes the NSF's upcoming 2026 Office of Metascience as a positive step and recommends the report's guidance for its development. Faherty, citing interviews and research, supports the report's conclusions and encourages the wider science community to do the same.
items.title: Matt Faherty Study Recommends Metascience for Federal Science Agencies

items.summary: At least eight people were killed and 17 injured when a bus carrying 25 devotees from Bhopal overturned on the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway in Kota district. Rescue operations are underway, with the district administration and locals assisting. Preliminary findings suggest the driver lost control, though the exact cause remains undetermined. A probe is ongoing to establish the circumstances of the accident.
items.title: Bus Carrying Khatu Shyam Devotees Overturns on Delhi-Mumbai Expressway in Kota

items.summary: Alistair Boxall, a professor at the University of York, leads a new study detecting widespread river contamination by pharmaceuticals and PFAS across Europe. The research found Spain ranks second in pharmaceutical concentrations, with the Henares River showing the highest risk due to antibiotic levels. Boxall notes that current regulations monitor fewer than 50 substances despite society using hundreds of thousands. He expresses surprise that no action is taken despite known risks to local ecology and human health, including antimicrobial resistance. The study highlights the need for better wastewater treatment and potentially new regulations.
items.title: Chemist Alistair Boxall Warns of Widespread River Contamination by Pharmaceuticals and PFAS

items.summary: Medellín has invested $165 million in tree planting since 2008, transforming 18 roads into green corridors. However, rising temperatures and unequal distribution of vegetation leave vulnerable areas like Villa Sofía exposed. Residents report unbearable heat without shade or air conditioning. Experts note that while high-income districts have green spaces, poorer neighborhoods lack them. Recent record-breaking temperatures highlight the urgent need for equitable climate adaptation measures across the city.
items.title: Medellín's Green Corridors Fail to Cool Vulnerable Neighborhoods Amid Rising Heat

items.summary: Sources familiar with the matter report that some Anthropic investors are considering a lower valuation for the AI company before its IPO. This shift follows financial disclosures showing a 45% revenue jump to $16.8 billion in the third quarter, though investors remain concerned about slowing sequential growth. The potential lower valuation comes as broader worries mount over the ballooning cost of financing AI development.
items.title: Anthropic Investors Consider Lower Valuation Ahead of IPO

items.summary: Tesla has opened online reservations for its new Roadster in India, featuring inspirations from the SR-71 and F-35 alongside SpaceX components. The vehicle will be available exclusively in Left-Hand Drive configurations starting in 2028. Additionally, customers can reserve a complimentary Acceleration Boost for the six-seater Model Y L alongside their Roadster booking.
items.title: Tesla Opens Reservations for New Roadster in India

items.summary: TCS and HCLTech reported significant increases in AI-related revenue, yet their total revenue growth remained limited. Experts suggest that while AI improves efficiency, it may also pressure pricing on legacy IT contracts, limiting overall financial gains.
items.title: TCS and HCLTech see AI revenue surge while overall growth slows

items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang expressed confidence that artificial intelligence's long-term economic benefits will outweigh current investor uncertainty following a recent selloff in AI stocks. While semiconductor stocks faced a prolonged decline and CoreWeave shares dropped 25%, Huang argued that short-term volatility would not alter the industry's fundamentals. He emphasized that AI remains in early development stages and will transform industries worldwide.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Maintains AI Growth Outlook Amid Market Turbulence

items.summary: Jack Clark, co-founder of Anthropic, stated that rapidly improving artificial intelligence will accelerate change across all fields. He cited an internal economic model forecasting US output could reach $44 trillion by 2030, a figure he acknowledged sounds outlandish but is implied by technological progress. Clark emphasized the need for international cooperation to establish serious rules for this transformative technology.
items.title: Anthropic's Clark Forecasts AI to Vastly Boost US GDP by 2030

items.summary: Apple advises users to back up their iPhones daily to protect against data loss from damage or theft. Many skip this due to iCloud storage limits or assumptions that data rarely changes. Automatic iCloud backups occur nightly when devices are plugged in and connected to Wi-Fi, though they often require a paid iCloud Plus subscription due to storage needs.
items.title: Apple Advises Daily iPhone Backups to Prevent Data Loss

items.summary: Analyst Sudeep Shah of SBI Securities discusses the Indian stock market outlook, noting a recent Nifty recovery driven by easing global headwinds and cooling US bond yields. He highlights strong performance in the Nifty IT sector and anticipates continued dominance by large-cap stocks, particularly banking heavyweights like HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, and Axis Bank, ahead of their earnings. Shah identifies key technical resistance levels for the Bank Nifty and suggests that sustained Foreign Institutional Investor buying could support further index gains, though a durable trend reversal remains unconfirmed.
items.title: Analyst Sudeep Shah Outlines Nifty IT and Banking Strategy

items.summary: The Financial Times reported that Anthropic is offering Blackstone a yield of more than 10% to finance a chip deal. Blackstone funds would invest $9 billion in debt backed by Anthropic's five-year lease payments, though Reuters could not immediately verify the report.
items.title: Anthropic Offers Blackstone High-Yield Financing for Chip Deal

items.summary: Apple Inc. stated that demand for the new iPhone Duo has been extraordinary following delivery delays extending into January. The company continues accepting orders and invites customers to Apple Stores. Bloomberg analysts estimate sales could exceed 14 million units, potentially raising the average selling price by 82% or 67% depending on customer switching behavior.
items.title: Apple Reports Extraordinary iPhone Duo Demand Amid Shipping Delays

items.summary: On October 17, 2026, 45 countries jointly released the Framework of World Vocational and Technical Education Standards, known as the Beijing Agreement, in Tianjin, China. Led by China, the framework promotes vocational education cooperation, lifelong learning, and artificial intelligence in teaching. During the event, China's Ministry of Education signed memorandums with 13 countries, while Chinese institutions signed agreements with 11 overseas institutions across six fields.
items.title: China Leads Global Vocational Education Framework Launch

items.summary: Anthropic has quietly pitched a draft AI safety Bill to US lawmakers, according to Politico. The proposal would allow the government to block model releases only if they pose a risk of over US$1 billion in damages or serious injury to more than 50 people. An Anthropic spokesperson stated the Bill reflects proposals from the company's 'Advanced AI Framework' released earlier this year.
items.title: Anthropic Proposes AI Safety Bill to US Lawmakers

items.summary: Chinese AI and technology stocks suffered heavy losses as a global market downturn threatened Beijing's financing ambitions. The Star50 Index fell nearly 40% in the current half-year, while the ChiNext Index declined 36%. Semiconductor firms lost half their value, and foreign investment outflows reached 90 billion yuan in the third quarter. Valuations remain elevated compared to international peers.
items.title: China's Tech Stocks Plunge Amid Global AI Downturn

items.summary: MK Stalin, the DMK chief, criticized the Congress party for alleged double standards regarding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. During a meeting of the DMK Parliamentary Party, Stalin and his party adopted resolutions demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and electoral reforms. The DMK accused Congress of opposing the SIR nationally while failing to raise similar objections in states like Kerala and Tamil Nadu. Stalin also highlighted internal troubles within the opposition alliance in Bihar, including seat-sharing disputes. Meanwhile, Rahul Gandhi claimed Congress was the first to raise concerns about the SIR process, stating that the truth was now emerging from within the Election Commission itself.
items.title: DMK Leader MK Stalin Criticizes Congress Over Electoral Roll Revision

items.summary: The Graham Act of 2026 authorized tariffs up to 100% on major Russian energy importers, including India, China, and Turkey, to pressure them to reduce purchases. However, on October 17, 2026, President Trump invoked a waiver provision to suspend these sanctions, citing national interests. The move aims to facilitate the release of Russian diesel into global markets to lower US fuel prices ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. While this provides immediate relief for affected nations, the legislative framework remains intact, preserving the option to restore measures later. The decision has drawn criticism from lawmakers who argue sanctions should be enforced to pressure Russia over Ukraine.
items.title: Trump pauses Russia sanctions to ease US diesel prices amid election

items.summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant addressed graduates at the National Law School of India University's 34th annual convocation in Bengaluru. He warned that external forces created uncertainty over the event. The CJI urged lawyers to uphold justice, maintain intellectual independence, and listen to differing viewpoints while defending what is just.
items.title: CJI Warns of External Forces Threatening NLSIU Convocation

items.summary: The Nifty index reclaimed its 200-week moving average at 22,651.47, preventing a deeper deterioration in its long-term technical structure. However, the recovery is not yet a confirmed trend reversal as the index remains below shorter-term moving averages. Indicators like the weekly RSI at 42.29 and bearish MACD suggest underlying momentum remains weak despite the recent recovery.
items.title: Nifty Reclaims 200-Week Moving Average Amid Weak Momentum

items.summary: China has approved four-year pilot programs for comprehensive hydrogen energy applications in five city clusters, according to a government circular released Friday. The initiative aims to expand cleaner energy use in industry and transport, with participating cities urged to accelerate implementation of priority tasks including fuel cell vehicle promotion and refueling station construction. Central government funds will support these efforts.
items.title: China Approves Hydrogen Pilot Programs in Five City Clusters

items.summary: Wall Street tumbled on Oct 16 as concerns over AI trade and rising oil prices weighed on markets. CoreWeave slumped 12%, while oil prices jumped over 3% due to Middle East supply worries. The Nasdaq faced a potential weekly loss exceeding 4%, driven by fears that debt-laden AI companies may struggle to repay debts as borrowing costs rise.
items.title: Wall Street Tumbles on AI Trade Worries and High Oil Prices

items.summary: China and Europe are establishing new aerospace connections that span both civil aviation and space exploration. Their deep industrial partnership is scaling global civil aviation, while scientific collaboration is opening possibilities for space exploration and deepening understanding of the Sun-Earth system. A video generated with AI assistance provides further details on these developments.
items.title: China and Europe Expand Aerospace Ties From Aviation to Space

items.summary: In an exclusive BizTalk interview, CGTN's Guan Xin spoke with Zlatko Lagumdzija, former prime minister of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Lagumdzija discussed China's development and its role in global governance, drawing on his firsthand experience from multiple visits to the country. He reflected on achievements in economic development, technological innovation, and green transition, while also discussing the vision for international cooperation behind the Belt and Road Initiative.
items.title: Former Bosnian PM Discusses China's Role in Global Governance

items.summary: TTD Executive Officer Muddada Ravichandra felicitated four cultural troupes during the Hanumantha Vahanam Seva at Tirumala on Saturday. As many as 516 artists from 25 cultural troupes representing 14 states showcased India's diverse cultural traditions through performances including Bharatanatyam, Maruni and Kommu Koya dances. The event added cultural splendour to the celebrations and captivated devotees who gathered in large numbers.
items.title: TTD Honours Cultural Troupes During Tirumala Brahmotsavams

items.summary: A book review examines Yiyun Li's memoir, Things in Nature Merely Grow, which details her intellectual approach to processing the suicide deaths of her two sons, James and Vincent. Li employs radical acceptance to navigate her grief, noting that the word 'grief' fails to capture her condition. The text highlights her specific coping mechanisms, such as repeating the phrase 'Children die and parents go on living,' while acknowledging the book serves as a tribute to her children and a resource for others facing loss.
items.title: Review of Yiyun Li's Memoir on Grief and Loss

items.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy stated that a supertanker carrying more than 2 million barrels of crude oil exploded and caught fire after striking a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz. According to Sepah News, the vessel took an unauthorized route, violating Iranian regulations. Press TV reported accusations that the tanker deliberately disabled its GPS and radar. The incident remains unverified. Amid heightened regional tensions, the IRGC warned of severe consequences for vessels defying its restrictions, linking the event to US deception. This follows a similar claim regarding a sinking cargo ship two days prior. The IRGC asserts the waterway remains closed under Tehran's sovereign decisions.
items.title: Iran Claims Supertanker Hit Mine in Strait of Hormuz

items.summary: The Grand Condé, a rare nine-carat pink diamond stolen in 1926, is on display in France for the first time in nearly 100 years. The museum's director, Mathieu Deldicque, noted that while the recovery story involving a maid and an apple may sound far-fetched, it was widely reported at the time. The exhibition runs until January 3, featuring academic analysis and archive material about the gem's history.
items.title: Rare pink diamond Grand Condé returns to display in France after century

items.summary: Pope Leo XIV is set to leave Rome's Gemelli Hospital following successful lung cancer surgery. Doctors confirmed he has adenocarcinoma and is fit for discharge based on recent tests. He will deliver a noon blessing from St Peter's Square on Sunday. His personal physician stated he is deemed fit. The Vatican announced plans for a trip to Latin America in November.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV Discharged After Lung Cancer Surgery

items.summary: A Patna court sentenced Naushad Ahmed to two years' rigorous imprisonment and fined him Rs 6,500 for pronouncing instant triple talaq. The court acquitted him of acid attack allegations. Ahmed's lawyer plans to challenge the verdict in the high court, noting this is the first such sentence in the district under the 2019 law.
items.title: Patna Court Sentences Man for Triple Talaq

items.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has released a draft amendment to ban sucrose and fructose in food for infants up to six months. Published on Friday, the 2026 regulations aim to strengthen nutritional requirements and align with public health guidance promoting exclusive breastfeeding. FSSAI seeks stakeholder feedback within 60 days before finalizing the changes.
items.title: FSSAI Proposes Ban on Added Sugars in Infant Food

items.summary: White House press secretary Katie Zacharia was dismissed mid-interview after Vice President JD Vance requested a chat. Trump advised her to reconsider the role. Zacharia, who served only five days, cited limited preparation time for her first briefing and faced scrutiny over her legal credentials. Her departure leaves the communications role vacant before the midterm elections.
items.title: Trump's Press Secretary Fired Mid-Interview After Brief Tenure

items.summary: The father of the doctor murdered at RG Kar Medical College questioned the CBI after the Supreme Court granted bail to former principal Sandip Ghosh in a financial irregularities case. This ruling intensified criticism from the victim's family and doctors involved in the justice movement, who demanded faster proceedings and accountability for alleged investigation lapses.
items.title: Victim's Father Questions CBI After Sandip Ghosh Supreme Court Bail

items.summary: Peter Ricketts, a former national security adviser, warned ministers to be honest with the British public about immediate Russian threats, including hybrid attacks on critical infrastructure that could cause casualties. He cited reckless cyber-assaults and called for increased investment in resilience. His comments align with recent warnings from MI5 and the British army regarding Moscow's aggression, which Ricketts described as the number one aggressor.
items.title: Former Security Adviser Urges Honesty on Russian Hybrid Threats

items.summary: A Mysuru fast-track court sentenced 32-year-old Karthik to death for raping and murdering a nine-year-old girl during the 2025 Dasara festival. The court found him guilty based on forensic evidence, including DNA test results and post-mortem reports. Former Mysuru MP Pratap Simha welcomed the verdict, noting the incident caused deep distress among residents.
items.title: Mysuru Court Sentences Man to Death for Rape and Murder of 9-Year-Old

items.summary: The Vatican announced that Pope Leo XIV has been cleared for discharge from Rome's Gemelli hospital following surgery to remove a cancerous growth from his lung. Doctors confirmed the procedure was successful with no complications, citing blood tests and a chest X-ray that showed good recovery. The pontiff is scheduled to return to the Vatican and lead the Angelus prayer.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV Cleared for Discharge After Lung Surgery

items.summary: The Vatican announced that Pope Leo XIV will leave Gemelli hospital on October 17 to return to the Vatican. Doctors deemed him fit for discharge following lung cancer surgery. He is 71 years old. The Pope will recite the Angelus prayer from the papal apartment the next day.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV to Leave Hospital and Return to Vatican

items.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has proposed a ban on adding sucrose and fructose to infant nutrition products intended for babies up to six months of age. Published as a draft amendment on October 16, the proposal seeks to strengthen existing regulations that currently allow these sugars under specific limits. FSSAI has invited objections and suggestions from stakeholders within 60 days of the notification's publication. The regulator notes that while the move aims to reduce unnecessary sugar exposure during a critical growth period, it does not guarantee prevention of childhood obesity. Existing rules remain in force until the amendment is finalized.
items.title: FSSAI Proposes Ban on Added Sugars in Infant Foods Under Six Months

items.summary: Experts state that Indian refiners reduced Russian oil purchases before Donald Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act on September 18. While the US granted a temporary waiver from potential 100% tariffs, industry sources note that refiners have already cut Russian crude imports by a third since July. Consequently, India's crude import bill rose 31.6% in September as refiners shifted to more expensive supplies from the US and other regions. Ajay Srivastava of the Global Trade Research Initiative argues the waiver offers no long-term assurance, noting that secondary sanctions remain active and could be used as leverage in future trade negotiations.
items.title: Indian Refiners De-risked Ahead of US Sanctions Waiver

items.summary: Madeline Horwath is the subject of a cartoon titled 'Madeline Horwath on AI food advertising – cartoon'. The item presents this title as a single sentence without further elaboration, context, or supporting details regarding the content of the cartoon or the specific nature of the discussion.
items.title: Madeline Horwath Discusses AI Food Advertising in a Cartoon

items.summary: At the IMF's annual meeting in Bangkok, policymakers noted the surprising resilience of the global economy despite geopolitical chaos and high oil prices. However, the IMF cautioned that this resilience may not last, citing the high cost of energy support measures and unsustainable public finances in advanced economies. The organization highlighted risks of an AI market crash and urged governments to repair fiscal deficits. While some markets showed signs of stress, including a significant drop in South Korea's Kospi index and US tech stocks, the IMF warned that the current stability rests on shaky foundations.
items.title: IMF Warns Global Economy Resilience May Be Shaky Amid Fiscal and AI Risks

items.summary: Euronews released a news bulletin on October 17th, 2026, offering a brief overview of global stories. The broadcast covers world affairs, business, politics, culture, entertainment, and travel. Described as independent and European, the program aims to provide a reliable context for current events. It serves as a regular update for viewers worldwide.
items.title: Latest news bulletin | October 17th, 2026 – Midday

items.summary: A heavy reinforcement cage fell onto a moving car at the Anand Nagar–Saket Elevated Road project site on Kopri Bridge in Thane. The Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority imposed a Rs 2 crore penalty on the contractor for the safety lapse. No injuries were reported, but the incident prompted an investigation into construction practices and safety procedures at the site.
items.title: MMRDA fines contractor Rs 2 crore after reinforcement cage falls on car

items.summary: A diplomat reported that all seven candidates for the UN secretary-general position received a 'discourage' vote, effectively a veto, from a permanent Security Council member in an informal straw poll. Rebeca Grynspan led in 'encourage' votes but also faced vetoes. US envoy Mike Waltz declined to comment on reports of opposition but emphasized the need for the best candidate. The outgoing secretary-general, Antònio Guterres, ends his term on December 31, 2026.
items.title: Seven UN Candidates Receive Veto in Informal Security Council Poll

items.summary: Qcells announced plans to introduce U.S.-made aluminum frames for its residential solar panels by the end of 2026. Partnering with Aluko Group, the initiative aims to help installers qualify for a 10% tax credit bonus under Treasury Department guidance. The frames will be manufactured in Halls, Tennessee, supporting clean energy projects as domestic content thresholds rise toward 55% for construction starting in 2027.
items.title: Qcells and Aluko Group Partner for U.S. Solar Frame Production

items.summary: Donald Trump blocked numerous Russia sanctions two days before they were set to take effect, citing national interest. This move followed a controversial deal to import Russian diesel, which Ukraine accused the administration of supporting Russia's war effort. Relations have frayed as Trump criticized Zelensky, while Zelensky condemned the waiver and resumed strikes on Russian energy infrastructure. Democrats criticized the decision as a betrayal of Ukraine. Meanwhile, Trump denied halting intelligence sharing or slowing the Starlink network, despite reports of disruptions affecting Ukraine's ability to defend against Russian attacks. The situation remains tense as both nations exchange sharp words.
items.title: Trump Waives Russia Sanctions Amid Escalating Row With Zelensky

items.summary: Police in Gurugram suspect Mohammad Aslam killed his wife Farhana before committing suicide. Investigators found a note stating 'We are leaving this world' and recovered electronic devices for forensic analysis. A murder case was registered under Section 103(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. Autopsies are pending, and relatives express shock over the sudden deaths of the couple, who had no prior marital discord.
items.title: Gurugram Police Suspect Murder-Suicide Involving IT Couple

items.summary: While AI adoption in the U.S. workplace has surged, experts warn that reliance on flawed AI output can lead to professional liability. Unlike developers, professionals using AI remain responsible for errors, such as fabricated citations or inaccurate data, which have already triggered lawsuits and fines. The article highlights the tension between leveraging AI efficiency and maintaining independent professional judgment.
items.title: Companies May Be Liable for AI Errors

items.summary: Brazil's new curtailment rules are unlikely to immediately revive utility-scale solar investment, according to a study by the Brazilian Solar Photovoltaic Energy Association (ABsolar). Despite offering greater certainty, high curtailment rates and compensation uncertainty remain decisive factors. In 2026 alone, developers surrendered authorizations for 923 solar projects, representing over 40.6 GW of capacity and BRL 134 billion in lost investment. While regulatory clarity has improved, experts like Eduardo Tobias of Watt Capital note that investment recovery depends on complex variables like electricity demand growth and storage deployment, making new greenfield projects an exception rather than the rule for now.
items.title: Brazil's New Curtailment Rules Unlikely to Revive Solar Investment

items.summary: Wallaroos captain Siokapesi Palu Sekona stated her team has room for improvement following a 56-12 win over Scotland. While the victory snapped a losing streak, Sekona and coach Tim Walsh emphasized the need to refine discipline and set-pieces. The team aims to become the best in the world, with a shift to full-time status planned before the 2029 World Cup.
items.title: Wallaroos captain seeks world-class status despite victory

items.summary: Cartoonist Amruta Patil curated the exhibition 'A Moving Line' at MAP Bengaluru, presenting over 250 works that span millennia of Indian visual storytelling. The show juxtaposes ancient artifacts like temple carvings and scrolls with modern comics to challenge the notion that sequential art is a Western invention. Patil argues that indigenous traditions have long utilized sequenced images, serving as a witness to national history. The exhibition aims to historicize Indian graphic narratives in a context where such heritage is often undervalued or lost. Patil, who published India's first queer graphic novel, 'Kari', in 2008, views the project as a gift to the community, emphasizing the need to preserve diverse cultural stories against homogenization and colonial perspectives.
items.title: Cartoonist Amruta Patil Curates Exhibition on Indian Graphic Narrative History

items.summary: Mitchell Moses, a halfback for the Kangaroos, will miss the remainder of the Rugby League World Cup after sustaining a calf injury. The injury occurred during Australia's tournament opener against the Tigers, which ended in a 6-0 loss. Moses was ruled out of the title defence, while Papua New Guinea began their tournament with victories.
items.title: Mitchell Moses Ruled Out of World Cup Due to Calf Injury

items.summary: The article reports that half of Donald Trump's eight female cabinet officials have resigned or been fired during his second term, all replaced by men. Notable departures include press secretary Katie Zacharia, homeland security secretary Kristi Noem, attorney general Pam Bondi, and labor secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer. While some male officials like Pete Hegseth and Kash Patel faced scrutiny, they remain in post. Democrats argue this highlights a double standard, noting that male officials are often rewarded for misconduct. Trump previously stated he is not a feminist but supports everyone. The piece details specific reasons for departures, such as controversies over immigration enforcement, the Epstein files, and internal investigations.
items.title: Trump Cabinet Sees High Turnover Among Female Officials

items.summary: A severe sewage odor from Thames Water drains has forced the Bicycle Nation shop in Herne Hill, south London, to restrict operations and move mechanics outside. Owner Tamas Polocz reported that the smell, described as unbearable and resembling rotten eggs, has affected staff health and business viability. While Thames Water accepted liability for the issue stemming from a mains sewer beneath the shop, it has not provided a resolution date. Experts suggest the problem is linked to dry conditions and a lack of rain to flush the system. The incident has renewed calls for an overhaul of London's aging Victorian sewage infrastructure, which is ill-equipped for current climate conditions.
items.title: Thames Water Sewer Stench Disrupts South London Bike Shop Operations

items.summary: Although AI models like AlphaGenome aim to predict biological traits from DNA sequences, experts argue that the human genome is not a static blueprint but a highly dynamic, context-dependent system. Biologists Karen Adelman and Wendy Bickmore explain that gene regulation involves complex, overlapping mechanisms, including three-dimensional chromatin folding and noncoding enhancers, which cannot be fully captured by simple input-output algorithms. The genome functions as a responsive, adaptive organ influenced by evolution, environment, and internal cellular conditions rather than a predictable program. Consequently, while AI may offer useful predictions, it lacks the capacity to discern the fundamental principles governing this intricate, self-referential biological system without human reasoning.
items.title: Why AI Struggles to Decode the Complex, Dynamic Nature of Human Genomes

items.summary: Weddings are increasingly expensive, with average costs reaching $36,000, prompting couples to seek savings on cakes. While specialty bakers charge over $1,000, grocery chains like Publix and Costco offer cheaper alternatives. Anna Holleran and Lily Alana Stewart chose grocery cakes to save money, noting that while options are fewer, the tradition remains important. Zola reports that about a third of couples consider spending less on dessert.
items.title: Couples Turn to Grocery Stores for Cheaper Wedding Cakes Amid Rising Costs

items.summary: French students are protesting demanding better learning conditions and investment in public education, citing crumbling infrastructure exacerbated by record heat waves. Cléo, a 16-year-old student, described experiencing heat exhaustion in classrooms during France's second consecutive heat wave. The protests have led to roughly 8,000 arrests in three weeks, with 85 percent of them minors. Students highlight issues like falling ceilings and moldy walls, while experts note schools were not designed for hotter climates. The Île-de-France region allocated $1.2 billion for renovations, yet many worry about the long-term impacts of climate change on their future.
items.title: French Students Protest Heat-Unsafe Schools Amid Climate Crisis

items.summary: Families in Delhi sleep on sidewalks outside major hospitals like AIIMS and Safdarjung because they cannot afford lodging while relatives receive critical treatment. Many traveled hundreds of miles from states like Bihar and Madhya Pradesh, often leaving work and education behind. While hospitals offer financial aid for treatment, they do not explicitly cover lodging costs, leaving families to rely on charity or makeshift shelters. Volunteers distribute food, but many still go hungry. Patients and caregivers face uncertainty, heat, and safety concerns, with some waiting weeks or months for treatment plans. One hospital did not respond to requests for comment on the accommodation crisis, though its website mentions assistance with dharamshalas. The situation highlights a gap between medical care access and the ability to stay near treatment facilities.
items.title: Families Sleep on Delhi Sidewalks While Loved Ones Receive Hospital Care

items.summary: A study by the Center for Biological Diversity indicates that approximately 25 percent of rivers in the continental United States contain levels of atrazine harmful to wildlife and human health. Nathan Donley, the study's author, notes this affects nearly a million miles of waterways, with hotspots in the Corn Belt and the Chesapeake Bay watershed. While atrazine is banned in 63 countries, including the European Union, it remains widely used in the U.S. on corn, sorghum, and sugarcane. The Biden administration's 2024 mitigation plan was analyzed by the Center for Biological Diversity and found insufficient, potentially remedying only 1 percent of contaminated rivers. Syngenta, the main manufacturer, stated the herbicide is safe when used according to label instructions, though the Center for Biological Diversity filed a lawsuit against the EPA regarding waterway protection.
items.title: Study Finds Atrazine in Quarter of US Rivers

items.summary: Iran denied involvement in Houthi attacks on Saudi targets, including a missile strike on Aden airport. Houthi rebels claimed responsibility for the strikes, targeting the Saudi-led coalition. While Saudi Arabia and Riyadh accused Tehran of orchestrating the escalation, Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei rejected these claims, stating that such assertions are not credible. Iran offered to mediate the conflict but emphasized that escalating tensions serves no party's interest.
items.title: Iran Denies Involvement in Houthi Attacks on Saudi Targets

items.summary: The International Monetary Fund reports that Bangladesh's per capita GDP is projected to exceed India's in 2026, with figures of $2,886 and $2,749 respectively. While India led in 2025 and is expected to regain the lead by 2029, the latest World Economic Outlook indicates a shift in the economic ranking for the two nations in the near term.
items.title: IMF Forecasts Bangladesh Surpasses India in Per Capita GDP by 2026

items.summary: Daniel Raim, a Los Angeles-based documentary director, has released 'The Ozu Diaries,' a film tracing the life of Yasujiro Ozu. Following his earlier work on Robert F. Boyle, Raim approaches this subject with admiration. The film premiered at the Venice International Film Festival and has screened at the 38th Tokyo International Film Festival and the Udine Far East Film Festival in Italy, receiving critical praise for its examination of Ozu as both a man and an artist.
items.title: Documentary Director Daniel Raim Explores Yasujiro Ozu's Legacy

items.summary: The Supreme Court rejected blanket age-based internet restrictions for children, affirming their fundamental right to access the internet. The court warned that such bans could drive minors to unregulated platforms and discourage them from seeking help for online abuse. Instead, it called for a regulatory framework that prioritizes safety measures, such as faster removal of harmful content, while preserving children's freedom to use the internet.
items.title: Supreme Court Rejects Age-Based Internet Ban for Children

items.summary: Mass rallies occurred across France on Saturday, addressing grievances such as high prices, social inequality, and a dilapidated education system. These protests follow an initial wave regarding school conditions. President Emmanuel Macron called for calm, while authorities estimate nearly 200,000 attendees. Restrictions were imposed on rallies near the Elysee palace and the Champs-Elysee avenue. Fears of violence persist, with Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu noting a moment of national fatigue.
items.title: France Braces for Nationwide Protests Amid Social Grievances

items.summary: Wisye Sahambangung, a community leader from Sarawet, North Sulawesi, leads Rhizopora, a women's group established in 2022 to restore mangroves and generate income. The group collects propagules, supplies seedlings, and monitors coastal areas. During a recent eight-month project, Rhizopora planted 30,000 mangrove trees in collaboration with NGOs Yayasan Bumi Tangguh and CARE Indonesia. Members sell seedlings and mud crabs, with prices ranging from 2,000 rupiah per seedling to 350,000 rupiah per kilogram of crabs. Sahambangung recently represented the group at the Women Deliver 2026 forum in Melbourne, highlighting how conservation supports local livelihoods.
items.title: Indonesian Women Lead Mangrove Restoration and Create Livelihoods

items.summary: A study involving sixteen AI agents, each given 1,000 satoshis of real bitcoin, found that four agents roughly doubled their money while two were wiped out. After a hundred rounds, the three richest agents held more than half of the bitcoin. An independent developer ran the experiment using 8 Claude agents and 8 GPT-4o agents, verifying that the agents discovered exploitative strategies without explicit rules. The raw payment data is public.
items.title: AI Agents Compete for Bitcoin in Real-World Study

items.summary: Scientists have observed orcas ramming heavy sunfish with enough force to cause the fish to literally explode on two separate occasions. While the exact reason for this behavior remains unknown, researchers suggest the orcas might be portioning food to feed their pod or simply acting out of boredom. Scientists plan to continue observing these events to better understand the phenomenon.
items.title: Scientists Observe Orcas Ramming Sunfish Until They Explode

items.summary: Domestic brokerage PL Capital lists eight small and midcap stocks with potential upside ranging from 13% to 50%. The firm maintains a cautious outlook for the near term, noting the Nifty trades at a discount to its long-term average multiple.
items.title: PL Capital Lists 8 Small-Midcap Stocks With Up To 50% Upside
